name: Sovereigntism
summary: Sovereigntism holds that a nation should keep supreme authority over its own laws, borders and policy, and resist transfer of that authority to supranational bodies such as the EU, the UN or international courts. Its adherents argue that legitimate power rests on the consent of a national people and that global governance escapes democratic accountability. It is mostly a stance on where authority sits, so its economic and social positions differ by strand, though the best-known contemporary versions are right-leaning and favour border control, protectionism and cultural continuity.
scope: The anti-supranational, nation-state-centred sense of sovereigntism as it appears in Euro-Atlantic politics today: US 'new sovereigntism' and Trump-era rejection of 'globalism', British Eurosceptic sovereigntism from Thatcher's Bruges speech to Brexit, and French and other continental 'Europe of nations' parties such as the Rassemblement National. It excludes the Quebec independence movement (covered by quebec-nationalism) and the Russian and 'archeo-sovereigntist' variants. Because the doctrine is about the level of authority rather than a full programme, most economic and social answers are low-confidence or neutral.

keyFigures.role: British prime minister whose 1988 Bruges speech opposed a European superstate and became a Eurosceptic rallying point.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Sovereigntism is about who holds authority, not welfare design; right sovereigntists (Trump) and left ones (Quebec, left Eurosceptics) split on state healthcare.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No sovereigntist source takes a line on wage floors; left variants favour them, right variants distrust them.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Wikipedia notes leftist sovereigntists use borders against free-market neoliberalism while others are market-friendly, so adherents split.

public-ownership.rationale: Left sovereigntists accept public ownership of strategic sectors while right ones prefer private firms; no common doctrine.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not a sovereigntist question; positions follow each strand's economic left-right placement and cancel out.

unions-good.rationale: Left sovereigntists defend unions as against globalised capital, right ones are cool toward them; the core doctrine is silent.

property-fundamental.rationale: The constitutionalist strand frames national constitutions and consent of the governed as supreme, which tends to include property rights, but it is inferred rather than stated.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Sovereigntists dislike transnational corporations but right variants resist regulation, so it is split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Wikipedia links sovereigntism with protecting national populations and welfare chauvinism; adherents tend to defend welfare for citizens while limiting it for outsiders.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not part of sovereigntist doctrine and alien to its conservative mainstream; only some left-wing strands would endorse it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Border and security emphasis in the Trump speech suggests tolerance of state security powers, but surveillance is not addressed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Trump's speech ties border enforcement to fighting criminal gangs and drug flows; the mainstream strand leans prohibitionist, inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The conservative strand objects to international human-rights bodies imposing speech norms; it is an inference, not a documented stance.

strong-leader.rationale: Wikipedia links sovereigntism to leaders like Orban and Trump who override constraints, but adherents are mixed since constitutionalists value checks.

state-harmful.rationale: Sovereigntists treat the democratic nation-state as the highest form of political organisation, so calling it harmful contradicts their core.

limit-guns.rationale: US sovereigntists defend the Constitution's supremacy, including against international arms control, which wikipedia lists among opposed agreements.

empower-police-military.rationale: Emphasis on national security, border control and a self-reliant state suggests support, though it is inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The conservative mainstream is socially traditional; sex work is not addressed by sources, so this is inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Sovereigntists want decisions at the national level against supranational bodies, but some US strands also favour decentralisation; genuinely split on the level below the nation.

rehabilitation.rationale: No sovereigntist doctrine on penal policy; strands differ.

traditional-family.rationale: Wikipedia cites Hungary's family policy and emphasis on cultural identity among right sovereigntists, but it is not core to the ideology.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Right-sovereigntist governments such as Hungary have opposed it, while Quebec sovereigntists favoured it; mainstream inference lean is against.

abortion-legal.rationale: Strands split: Trump-era US and Hungary lean restrictive, Quebec and French sovereigntists accept legal abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not doctrinal; some strands invoke religion and tradition, others (French laicite) defend secularism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Sovereigntists object to international human-rights bodies pressing remedies on states; Wikipedia notes US minorities seeking redress via international norms are seen as threats to majority sovereignty.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The conservative strand emphasises traditional identity and is hostile to gender minority claims per Wikipedia; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Wikipedia describes sovereigntism as emphasising cultural identity and taking back control to protect the nation's distinct character.

gradual-change.rationale: Thatcher-style sovereigntism defends established national institutions, but archeo-sovereigntists seek radical return to a prior order.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Right-wing sovereigntists see borders as filters against immigrants and Orban's Hungary is cited; left Quebec-style variants are less restrictive.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Trump's UN speech rejects global governance, the ICC and international bodies unaccountable to citizens; Wikipedia lists opposition to UN, EU power concentration.

free-trade.rationale: Wikipedia says sovereigntism leans protectionist and the Trump speech demands fair and reciprocal trade rather than free trade; Thatcher-style market sovereigntists dissent.

nation-first.rationale: Trump says the nation chooses independence over global governance and rejects globalism for patriotism; Wikipedia defines it as taking back control.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Trump says the US will not tell other countries how to live and honours each nation's sovereignty; the sovereignty principle opposes interference.

open-borders.rationale: Trump declares border enforcement central and that migration policy is each nation's own, and sovereigntism treats borders as essential.

limit-growth.rationale: Sovereigntists stress national economic strength and jobs; growth limits are not a theme, inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Wikipedia lists opposition to multilateral climate agreements among US sovereigntist positions, and the Trump-era strand rejects them.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Sovereigntist sources say nothing on technological optimism, and its strands span techno-nationalists and traditionalists, so a neutral answer.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy independence is valued but nuclear is not discussed; strands split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Constitutionalist sovereigntists defend consent-based lawful order; revolution is not a theme and is inferred against.

experts-over-public.rationale: Sovereigntists object to networks of judges, lawyers and international bureaucrats governing outside national democratic control.

central-planning.rationale: Not doctrinal; the dominant strands are market or nationalist-capitalist, with left sovereigntists a minority.

socialized-markets.rationale: Left sovereigntists might accept it, right ones not; split.

land-value-tax.rationale: No source links sovereigntism to land taxation; it is a fiscal-design question on which its adherents have no common view.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not a sovereigntist question; strands diverge on economics.

basic-income.rationale: Unconditional income is not discussed by sovereigntist sources, and right strands favour work conditions while left ones may not, so split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trump's speech defends tariffs on China and fair-and-reciprocal trade, and Wikipedia says the movement tends toward protectionism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Hungary and Trump-era industrial policy suggest some openness, but market sovereigntists dissent.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Distributist ownership ideas are absent from sovereigntist sources; adherents have no shared stance on how property is distributed.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing money and wages is outside any sovereigntist strand, which keep national economies with borders and currencies.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Some sovereigntists distrust the ECB and other supranational finance, but abolition goes beyond a documented position.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; no source links sovereigntism to state-recognised bargaining bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Constitutionalist sovereigntism rests on consent of the governed and democratic accountability; one-party rule contradicts it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Thatcher-type British sovereigntists accept monarchy; republican and Quebec strands do not; the doctrine is indifferent.

democracy-best.rationale: The sovereigntist argument is that democratic legitimacy rests in the nation-state, though Hungarian illiberal strands qualify liberal democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Popular sovereignty is invoked and referendums are a favoured tool against EU integration, but representative constitutionalists dissent.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils replacing parliaments are contrary to the national constitutional order that sovereigntists defend.

right-to-secede.rationale: Quebec-style sovereigntists claim it, while other strands such as US and French sovereigntists protect existing national unity; split by strand.

natural-rulers.rationale: Consent of the governed is the sovereigntist basis of legitimacy, which rules out natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream strands accept lawful force by states but no doctrine either way.

war-builds-character.rationale: Trump's speech calls for peaceful cooperation among sovereign states; glorifying war is not documented.

separate-church-state.rationale: Strands split between French secularism and religious-identity sovereigntists.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Sovereigntists ground legitimacy in national constitutions and consent, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The doctrine centres on the sovereign state holding legal and security authority; private provision conflicts with it.

military-superiority.rationale: Trump's emphasis on a strong and self-reliant nation implies it, but isolationist strands disagree.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Wikipedia notes right strands hostile to minorities, but civic Quebec and constitutionalist strands define nation by consent; split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nation rather than class is the sovereigntist unit; left sovereigntists would be a partial exception.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not doctrinal; mainstream right sovereigntism leans against.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Authority within a state is taken to rest in national government; not discussed, inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Trump refuses obligations enforced by international bodies and ties aid to benefit; reparations are not discussed, inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Sovereigntism opposes pooling power across nations; Wikipedia describes defence of the Westphalian nation-state against integration.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Nations putting their interests first is endorsed, but individual egoism is not addressed.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; strands split between communitarian right and constitutional rights defenders.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Sovereigntism is silent on environmental philosophy, so adherents have no shared view on nature's intrinsic worth.

limit-population.rationale: Pronatalist Hungarian-style policy and nationalist worries about decline lean against limits, inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream sovereigntists are pro-industry nationalists.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Nothing in sovereigntist sources concerns pace of technological change, and the conservative strand is wary of disruption while others are pro-innovation, so neutral.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bioethics of enhancement is outside the doctrine, and no strand has an agreed line.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Sovereigntists want democratic national accountability and oppose unaccountable technocratic authority, inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption policy is not addressed by the sources; security-minded and liberty-minded sovereigntists would differ.

restore-past-order.rationale: Archeo-sovereigntists want a return to a pre-WWII order, but conservative and neo-sovereigntists do not; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Sovereigntists are ideologically committed to national control, but Trump-era pragmatism praises outcomes; the doctrine takes no stance on this general maxim.

direct-action.rationale: The constitutionalist mainstream works through national elections and legislatures, inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: A Gandhian or anarchist maxim about method; sovereigntist sources do not address it.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No sovereigntist strand advocates abandoning the nation-state or modern society.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Entirely outside sovereigntist doctrine, which keeps national economies.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not doctrinal; left sovereigntists might lean toward it, mainstream does not.

production-for-use.rationale: Not doctrinal; mainstream strands accept market production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist exploitation theory is not part of the mainstream sovereigntist view.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Conflicts with consent of the governed and national constitutionalism.

collective-farming.rationale: Not part of any strand and opposed by the market-oriented mainstream.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Trump's speech blames states such as Iran and China, not capitalism; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Sovereigntists defend state authority and taxation by consent of the governed, though libertarian-leaning US adherents dissent.

harm-principle.rationale: Mill's limit on state power is not endorsed or rejected by sovereigntist sources, and conservative and liberal strands differ on moral legislation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Not addressed; Quebec strand stresses collective rights, US strand individual constitutional rights.

conscription.rationale: Sources are silent; Gaullist and Nordic-style strands accept national service while Anglo ones prefer volunteers, so split.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Sovereigntists emphasise democratic voice within the nation, inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Neither endorsed nor rejected in sovereigntist sources; citizens-as-customers is a market-libertarian idea that only part of the right holds.

positive-liberty.rationale: Material-means notion of freedom is not addressed; right strands reject it while left strands accept, so adherents divide.

media-academia-power.rationale: Wikipedia and the CFR describe sovereigntists as suspicious of a coalition of NGOs, lawyers and bureaucrats, though universities and media are not directly named.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Mainstream sovereigntism is civic or cultural, and race science is not part of it, inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Sovereigntists defend existing national constitutional representation, inferred.

total-state.rationale: Constitutionalist sovereigntism limits government by a constitution recognising consent and rights.

national-rebirth.rationale: Archeo-sovereigntists and Trumpism invoke renewal, but moderate strands do not; split.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Wikipedia notes sovereigntism has been used to justify violating others' sovereignty (Russia), but the mainstream defends borders and the Westphalian order.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Contrary to constitutional authority based on consent.

bound-labor.rationale: Contrary to the constitutional liberal-democratic order the doctrine defends.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not doctrinal; mainstream adherents hold conventional views of knowledge, inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Sovereigntists reject externally imposed norms but do not dispute moral universality as such.

single-common-good.rationale: Constitutional sovereigntists emphasise democratic contestation, inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: National self-determination logic is sympathetic but sovereigntism does not take a Middle East line.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; Hungary and Israel-type practices exist, but the doctrine does not require it.

revive-national-language.rationale: Strong in Quebec and Corsica, absent in US and UK strands; split.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not doctrinal; mainstream market-oriented sovereigntists are against.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not part of the doctrine; right strands favour vouchers while left and Quebec strands favour public schooling.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not part of the doctrine, and it includes both austerity-minded Thatcherites and spending-minded populists.

economic-freedom.rationale: Thatcher ties free enterprise to national independence but left sovereigntists reject it; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: The doctrine rests on law and constitutions, inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Wikipedia defines sovereigntism as favouring political independence of a nation and taking back control.

force-without-un.rationale: Trump rejects global governance and holds the nation sovereign, so UN approval is not seen as binding, though isolationists dissent.

reason-over-faith.rationale: No source takes a position on epistemology; some strands are religious and others secular.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Right sovereigntists treat borders as filters and prioritise citizens; Trump ties aid to national benefit.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed directly; welfare-chauvinist right strands lean toward conditions but left sovereigntists do not, so split.

class-collaboration.rationale: Sovereigntism emphasises national unity over class but the sources do not discuss labour-employer relations, so inferred and neutral.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Sovereigntism emphasises preserving cultural identity and heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Russian and neo-sovereigntist strands favour such a front, while Western strands do not; split.

workers-nation.rationale: The nation is the sovereigntist unit and left sovereigntists favour national protection of workers, inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Hungary-type strands emphasise it, others do not.

ban-interest.rationale: Not part of any strand; sovereigntists accept national finance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not part of sovereigntism, which is documented as nation- and culture-focused, though hostile to minorities in some strands.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist theory of the state conflicts with the sovereigntist view that the nation-state expresses democratic consent, so mild disagreement.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Trump's speech denounces OPEC price rises and prizes energy independence, supporting domestic production.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Cultural-identity emphasis implies integration expectations, inferred, with Quebec strand favouring interculturalism.

elite-replacement.rationale: Some far-right strands hold it, but it is not the mainstream view.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not a sovereigntist topic; strands range from British first-past-the-post defenders to continental PR parties.

national-mission.rationale: Trump says the US will not tell other countries how to live and honours each nation's customs; sovereigntism is anti-universalist.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Sovereigntists on the cultural right deny that society systematically disadvantages women, though the doctrine itself does not address it.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Sovereigntists portray elites as selling out national control, though this is populist framing not doctrine.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is not part of any sovereigntist programme.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Sovereigntists reject outside bodies such as the ICC judging national forces, so accountability would be domestic only.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Sources say nothing on the size of government; libertarian-leaning US adherents agree while French and Hungarian state-activists reject.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No sovereigntist source advocates this; its mainstream defines the nation culturally or civically, not racially.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Not directly contested; sovereigntists object to external enforcement more than to equal worth, but some strands discriminate by nationality.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with no sovereigntist position.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Sovereigntists treat existing states as legitimate sovereign units, so they would not generally label them colonial projects.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Indian-specific issue unaddressed by sovereigntist sources; national uniformity is plausible but the strands do not take a stated view.

restrict-conversion.rationale: No sovereigntist source supports restrictions on conversion; the doctrine concerns state authority, not religious practice.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A South Asian religious-nationalist demand not part of sovereigntism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Strands split between secular French and religious Hungarian.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist notion not addressed here.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Sovereigntists hold that legitimate authority rests with the people organised in the nation-state (s2); the cited text does not state the consent principle itself.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trump's speech frames trade as fair and reciprocal and decries deficits, implying support for export surpluses.

population-transfer.rationale: Wikipedia notes hostility to minorities in some strands, but forced transfer is not mainstream, inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The libertarian principle is not part of the doctrine.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist themes appear in some nationalist writing but not sovereigntist sources, so neutral.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Militant democracy is not addressed; constitutionalists support it but Orban-type and US strands dispute it, so split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Freedom from outside domination is central to taking back control, but the statement concerns individuals.

separated-powers.rationale: US constitutional sovereigntists defend a constitution with checks and balances against external authority.

priority-to-poor.rationale: No sovereigntist source takes a stance on a preferential option for the poor; left and right strands diverge.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British policy associated with Thatcher, whose Bruges speech anchors sovereigntism, but non-British and left strands do not share it.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: A Thatcherite policy; right strands like it while left sovereigntists oppose, so split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Sources do not address; Malthusian views exist on the right but are not doctrine.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Wikipedia links right sovereigntism with cultural identity and hostility to outsiders, but it is not stated as doctrine.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Contrary to electoral accountability valued by sovereigntists.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; constitutionalists oppose but Hungarian-type governments use emergency rule.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price control is a left-leaning measure that market-friendly sovereigntists reject; nothing in the doctrine decides it.

party-controls-media.rationale: Contradicts the democratic accountability that underpins the sovereigntist argument.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Consistent with restrictive immigration and citizenship preferences of right strands.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: A socialist demand not in sovereigntist sources; populist strands may like it but it is not doctrinal.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party organisation is not addressed; sovereigntist parties range from disciplined (RN) to loose.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Wikipedia describes sovereigntism as opposing EU federalism and pooling of power in favour of a Europe of nations, and Thatcher's Bruges speech rejects a European superstate.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Constitutional design of executive power is not addressed beyond opposition to external authority; US and French strands accept presidential command, others not.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not a sovereigntist concern.

clerical-rule.rationale: Sovereigntism holds that authority rests on consent of the governed organised in the nation-state, which excludes clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The doctrine puts national interest and patriotism first.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; right strands lean toward moral concerns but constitutionalists defend speech.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Orban-type strands accept long tenure, constitutionalists oppose.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is not discussed in sources; populist strands like it but constitutionalists are cool.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Trump demands allies pay fair share, but does not end alliances; isolationists would agree, Atlanticists (Thatcher) disagree.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Compulsory home ownership is not found in any sovereigntist programme.

people-in-arms.rationale: Militia ideas appear in US strands but are not doctrine, and others favour professional armies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural nostalgia appears in some nationalist writing but sovereigntist sources do not take it up.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Self-determination logic supports reunification, but sources do not state it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist framing among right sovereigntists, not doctrinal.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Trump honours each nation's customs, implying respect for difference, but sovereigntists also defend their own as superior.

death-penalty.rationale: Mainstream right sovereigntists in the US defend it and reject external limits, but French and UK strands vary.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not doctrinal; religious-right strands favour, secular French and Quebec strands oppose.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; social conservatives favour restriction but libertarians and Quebec strands do not.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; some right sovereigntists favour ius sanguinis while US and Quebec strands accept birthright or civic citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Quebec sovereigntists support protecting French while other strands favour a dominant national language, so split by strand.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed by sovereigntist sources; adherents differ on accommodation.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Cultural identity emphasis suggests a conformity tilt, inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Trump ties aid to benefit to US, but sovereign debt is not addressed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Left sovereigntists link independence with economic transformation while right ones do not, so adherents split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Quebec's movement has discussed one while other strands defend existing constitutions.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Constitutionalist sovereigntism rests on consent of the governed, so adherents generally oppose curbing political freedoms for growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Trump says aid goes only to countries that respect the US and gets little in return; sovereigntists reject outside duties.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Gaullist-style French sovereigntism and neo-sovereigntists value national strategic autonomy; the Westphalian model implies it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; French sovereigntists accept it while parliamentary-system adherents do not.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Sovereigntists distrust unaccountable supranational bodies such as the ECB and favour democratic control, inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions are not addressed in sovereigntist sources.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Social-doctrine view of property is not addressed; right strands reject it, left ones accept.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist-dissident historical claim with no bearing on sovereigntism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Sovereigntists oppose external environmental regulation, inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Trump demands fair share and Thatcher backed NATO, but isolationists doubt it.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Respect for sovereignty implies it though Russian sovereigntism rejects.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not addressed; French secular strands support but religious-identity strands do not.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; strands include monarchist, presidential and parliamentary models.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Quebec strand rejects, central nation strands accept; split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One country two systems is not discussed in sovereigntist sources, and adherents are divided on regional autonomy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A divine ruler contradicts the consent-based legitimacy that sovereigntists invoke.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not addressed; Thatcherite and Hungarian right strands like flat taxes while others do not.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not a sovereigntist question; nature-nurture views vary across adherents.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The CFR notes sovereigntists defend constitutions that are the highest law, which binds the state.

space-expansion.rationale: Space goals are not addressed by sovereigntist sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed by sources; US constitutionalists admire the mixed constitution while others do not.

leader-cult.rationale: Constitutionalist sovereigntism opposes personality cults though populist strands accept visible leaders.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law is not addressed by sovereigntist sources, and adherents have no shared view.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine outside sovereigntism's concerns, so mild disagreement.

land-redistribution.rationale: Seizing estates is not part of mainstream sovereigntism, which keeps national property orders.

refugee-return.rationale: Right of return is not discussed; sovereigntists emphasise control of borders, so no clear stance.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Sovereigntism defends the Westphalian order, though Russian strand claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Contrary to the constitutional rights and consent-based order defended by sovereigntists.

women-must-cover.rationale: No sovereigntist source supports compulsory dress codes; this belongs to specific religious regimes.

common-currency.rationale: Opposing the euro is core to French and European sovereigntism and its rejection of EU integration.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Uniting peoples across borders contradicts the Westphalian nation-state defended by sovereigntists.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: A Central European minority-rights model not addressed by sovereigntist sources.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A Jewish-politics question not addressed by sovereigntism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is not a sovereigntist claim, and the doctrine tends to emphasise national will and identity.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is not addressed; nationalist strands accept national champions while market ones favour competition.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; Trump-era and Hungarian strands accept rescues of strategic firms while market-liberal ones do not.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Wikipedia notes that in the US minority redress through constitutional and international norms is seen as threatening majority sovereignty; Orban's strand curbs courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Conservative cultural strand opposes quotas, inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Archeo-sovereigntists lean this way, but mainstream does not.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding international standards would be external constraints on national policy, inferred from the rejection of global governance.

moral-incentives.rationale: A Maoist or Guevarist idea absent from sovereigntism.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foco theory is outside sovereigntism, and constitutionalists defend lawful order.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not addressed; British strands accept the Lords and monarchy, republican strands do not.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Cultural identity emphasis implies national-centred education.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Trump says the US will not tell other countries how to live, and sovereigntism respects each nation's independence.

patriotic-education.rationale: Trump's endorsement of patriotism as the opposite of globalism implies it.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Conservative right strands oppose it, inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not addressed, though some sovereigntists distrust private and supranational finance.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not addressed; a Marxist debate with no sovereigntist position.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Russian strand favours, others do not.

delink-world-market.rationale: Archeo-sovereigntists reject globalisation but mainstream do not.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian property absolutism is not part of the doctrine, and adherents differ on anti-discrimination law.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: US constitutional sovereigntists defend an entrenched constitution as supreme.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed, though a self-determination logic might support it.

elective-rulers.rationale: Consent of the governed implies elective rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Sovereigntists emphasise national majority consent, inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not addressed; constitutionalists accept legal resistance but the sources are silent.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty is central to UK Eurosceptic and Brexit sovereigntism but US constitutionalists reject it; split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Aristocratic duty is not addressed by sovereigntist sources.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Sovereigntism is an activist programme of reclaiming national control.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt School claim with no sovereigntist position, so neutral.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not addressed by sovereigntism, though its anti-elite populism sometimes echoes it.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Left strands agree but Trump-era ones frame it differently.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed; right strands might support it but the sources do not.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-movement question with no sovereigntist content.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Trump's speech says aid should go only to countries respecting the US and national independence is valued.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchism is not in sovereigntist sources; Westphalian sovereigntists defend current borders.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not a sovereigntist view; its focus is on the sovereignty of existing states over their territory.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; German and Italian strands differ on it.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Trump condemns communism strongly but fascism is not mentioned.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not a sovereigntist doctrine; only some US states-rights polemics make it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Wikipedia stresses sovereigntist emphasis on cultural identity, which suggests keeping national monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed by sovereigntist sources, though conservative strands often sympathise.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Trump honours the right of each nation to pursue its own customs, beliefs and traditions, and Wikipedia notes sovereigntist rejection of universal models.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not addressed; constitutionalists oppose political armies while Turkish or Russian strands support.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed by sovereigntist sources, with split strands on pay for domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed, though conservative strands generally accept it.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed by sovereigntist sources, and electoral principles favour election.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Wikipedia says protectionism and defending the nation against outside forces are typical, and Hungary and Trump policies restrict foreign takeovers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; traditionalist strands oppose while others accept.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandate is a council-democratic idea not in sovereigntist sources.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not addressed; Thatcherite strands accept while others prefer pay-as-you-go.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land held only for use is a socialist idea not in the doctrine.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary control of national budgets is the point of reclaiming sovereignty from Brussels, inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Quebec and French strands favour, others not.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Protective stance is consistent, Hungary restricts it.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The conservative strand objects to outcome-based discrimination rules, though sources do not address it.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed; traditionalist strands share some critique while market strands do not.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Trump says the US will not tell others how to live, but isolates Iran; Russian strand disagrees.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Honoring other nations' sovereignty is the central principle.

corporate-influence.rationale: Left sovereigntists decry corporate influence, right ones are more accepting of business, so split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Hungary's Sovereignty Protection Office was created to investigate foreign influence, per Wikipedia.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Hungary's family policy is noted as an example and prefers it to immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local purchase limits are not addressed, but protective strands (Hungary) have used them while others dislike.

job-guarantee.rationale: A left Keynesian idea; sovereigntist sources are silent and strands diverge.

democratic-peace.rationale: Trump says the US will not tell other countries how to live, so spreading democracy is rejected, but the empirical claim is not.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Sovereigntists ground legitimacy in consent and respect for national law, inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The new sovereigntists hold that the Constitution recognises no superior legal authority, and US ratification attaches reservations to preserve its supremacy.

non-intervention.rationale: Trump's UN speech honours each nation's right to chart its own path and not be told how to live, and neo-sovereigntists want powerful states restrained; Russian-style variants dissent.

industrial-unions.rationale: Sovereigntism has no doctrine on union structure; left strands and right strands differ, inferred from its focus on where authority sits.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mainstream sovereigntism frames its case as constitutional and democratic, not conspiratorial, though Wikipedia notes some strands are hostile to minorities; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; the cultural-continuity emphasis and conservative character of the best-known strands imply support for legal marriage, inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Sovereigntists criticise global governance for escaping democratic accountability, which implies support for citizen oversight of national government; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Wikipedia says sovereigntism leans toward protectionism and borders as defence against free-market neoliberalism, which favours national production over long supply chains; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Sovereigntist movements work through parties and governments such as the Rassemblement National, Brexit campaigns and Trump's party, not small informal groups; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Sovereigntism defines the nation by consent, constitution and culture rather than faith, though some strands such as Orban's invoke Christianity; split but mostly secular-civic.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Sovereigntists reject subordination to external authorities and stress equality of nation-states, as in Trump's UN speech; tribute is not discussed, so the answer is inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The doctrine concerns national, not regional, authority; its right and left strands differ on internal fiscal transfers.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Sovereigntism is silent on property regimes and its strands span left and right.

defeat-communism.rationale: Contemporary sovereigntists rarely frame a crusade against communism, and the strands split; no stated position.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed; sovereigntists span free-market and statist positions, with no common line on public service providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Sovereigntism is not a doctrine about religion, but right strands defend religion as national heritage; inferred as disagreement with the claim.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: No stated position; adherents range from free-market (Thatcher) to protectionist, so the sources give no common view.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; right-leaning adherents would reject it while left sovereigntists might accept it.

socialized-care.rationale: Right-leaning strands favour families doing care privately; inferred from their cultural-continuity emphasis, not stated.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism features in some French and other national-identity movements, but not in the sources for the doctrine; adherents are split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Sovereigntists stress national authority over treaties with outside bodies; treaties with internal nations are not addressed.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Sovereigntism is organised around the nation-state, markets and national identity, and not around common-property communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Border control and cultural continuity are stressed, but state settlement policy in minority regions is not addressed and strands differ.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Trump's speech and the Thatcher Bruges speech endorse free enterprise, while left strands do not; no common third-way claim.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: claims to national self-determination often rest on historical ties, though the doctrine is about authority, not land.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: Holocaust denial is not part of the doctrine.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine concerns the level of authority and strands differ on social policy.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred: sovereigntists ground legitimacy in the consent of a national people, which favours democratic pluralism.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: not addressed; strands are mostly liberal-democratic.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: it holds that power should rest on a people's own consent, which counts against ruling overseas territories for another's benefit.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: it relies on national consent rather than religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine is about national, not workplace or community, decision-making.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: right-leaning versions treat this framing as foreign to their emphasis on national unity.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred: social positions differ by strand.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: Trump's UN speech frames politics as patriots against globalists, not left against right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: right-leaning versions generally do not make this critique.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: strands differ; the Rassemblement National leans yes while others do not.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: It holds that legitimate power rests on the consent of a national people, not God.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred: economic positions differ by strand.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Keeping supreme authority over a nation's own policy includes its own defence.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: protectionist strands favour national development over global competition.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: it resists supranational bodies, but many adherents accept alliances such as NATO.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: hereditary succession conflicts with the national-consent basis of legitimacy sovereigntists claim.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: sovereigntism concerns where authority sits, and its adherents have no common view on banking structure.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Resisting transfer of authority to supranational bodies implies refusing conditions imposed by them, as in Trump's UN speech against global governance.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred: legitimacy rests on the consent of a national people, which sits badly with a wealth-based franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: right-leaning versions generally do not adopt ecofeminist critiques, and the doctrine itself is silent.

reification.rationale: Inferred: right-leaning sovereigntists generally reject Marxist-derived critiques of capitalism.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: right-leaning versions generally defend market ownership and see media bias differently, though the doctrine is silent.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: sovereigntism stresses democratic accountability and national law over foreign decree, so it favours rule through known national laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: Inferred: the national-people basis of sovereignty is mostly civic, though some strands such as the RN lean ethnic, so adherents are mixed toward disagreement.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: the doctrine is about the level of authority, with no stated position on online participation.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the complaint that supranational bodies escape accountability, which favours openness of national decision-making.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine is about authority, not religion, and right-leaning strands defend cultural continuity without restricting marriage by law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: it concerns national rather than religious identity, and most adherents would not endorse boycotts of minorities.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: sovereigntists favour national referendums and parliaments, and the doctrine has no position on randomly selected assemblies.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine says nothing about religious reinterpretation, and adherents range widely.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Sovereigntism is about the level of authority, and right and left strands differ on wealth; no common position can be inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The doctrine concerns supranational authority, not military personnel policy; strands differ, so no position is inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred from its defence of national self-government and traditional continuity; nothing in the sources has sovereigntists promoting state atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on border control and national security, which relies on police and prisons; sources do not address abolition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from its view that legitimate power rests on the consent of one national people, which sits uneasily with guaranteed communal shares.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Right strands favour private and community provision while left and Quebec strands back the welfare state; the doctrine itself is silent.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits fit the anti-elite populist strands, but the doctrine is about the level of authority and adherents are split.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national democratic accountability through existing representative institutions; delegable voting is not discussed.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to supranational bodies and its focus on national interest over global governance; not addressed directly.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious leadership is not an issue for the doctrine and adherents are split between traditionalists and liberals.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marital authority is outside the doctrine, and strands from traditionalist to secular differ on it.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Sovereigntists emphasise citizens as the sovereign body, so voting rights for foreign residents are inferred to be disfavoured; not stated in the sources.

rent-control.rationale: Sovereigntism concerns who holds authority, not housing policy; adherents split by left and right.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the defence of national law and economic interests; the sources do not address patents.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the civic-national orientation, which does not centre drilled youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Sovereigntism is about control of national authority and not weapons basing; adherents have no common position.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the demand that foreign authorities have no power on national territory; adherents split since some value alliances.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Recognition of genocide is not addressed by the sovereigntist sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Sovereigntism is not an economic doctrine and adherents split by left and right.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; sovereigntists broadly accept national and individual self-defence, so absolute pacifism is inferred to be rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the nation-state-centred view of history; the sources do not discuss national origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the largely conservative and national-popular variants in the scope; not addressed in the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the largely conservative and national-popular variants in the scope; not addressed in the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not addressed; the sources do not discuss martyrdom, and adherents differ.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Sovereigntism frames politics as a contest over authority and law, not a spiritual struggle; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not addressed; sovereigntism concerns the state's independence, with no stated order for culture and state.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Sovereigntism contests foreign and supranational control, not minority groups; adherents differ on the question.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the focus on existing nation-states and their borders, which this statement would redraw.

independent-unions.rationale: The doctrine concerns where authority sits, not union independence; left and right variants differ.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The best-known versions are right-leaning and do not make workers' power the test of socialism; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: No stance on service ownership; left variants favour public services, right variants do not.

second-chamber.rationale: The doctrine is about the national level, not chamber structure; adherents split.

municipal-property.rationale: Sovereigntism places authority in the nation-state and its people, not local communities, and favours no community ownership; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: It opposes handing decision power upward to joint bodies and favours authority at the national level; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split by left and right.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Right-leaning sovereigntists back national deregulation, such as Trump-era and post-Brexit regulatory autonomy; inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Emphasis on national control of borders and policy suggests the state should oversee payments; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Legitimacy rests on a national people's consent, but the sources do not address the worth of the person against the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not addressed; many adherents stress cultural continuity but the doctrine is silent.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty is central to the British version, where Parliament remains the final authority; inferred for regions.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Sovereigntism organises around the nation and its citizens, not race; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between civic and cultural versions.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Sources stress national self-rule, not rules for using force; adherents split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Civic sovereigntists (US, Britain) define the nation by citizenship, while some continental ones lean on shared language and culture, so adherents split.

communal-electorates.rationale: Sovereigntists hold that legitimacy rests on one national people's consent, which rules out separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Sovereigntists fear loss of authority to supranational bodies more than literal partition; some rhetoric points to foreign interference, so inferred and split.

free-public-college.rationale: Sovereigntism is silent on tuition and left and right strands differ.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Right-leaning sovereigntists reject carbon taxes and global climate regimes; left variants differ, so inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Stewardship is not a sovereigntist theme, though many invoke handing on a sovereign country to posterity; inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The doctrine takes no stance on gender and strands diverge.

arms-reduction.rationale: Sovereigntists stress national defence and distrust international arms-control treaties; inferred from their opposition to supranational constraints.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Sovereigntists criticise opaque supranational deals, favouring transparency, yet back executive freedom in diplomacy; adherents split.

capital-controls.rationale: Right sovereigntists favour free markets but protectionism, left ones back capital controls; no doctrine, so split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Sovereigntism stresses the national state's authority, though US strands also defend private gun ownership, so adherents are split; no source addresses it.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Sovereigntists regard defence of the nation as a core state function and its citizens' duty; inferred from Trump's and Thatcher's patriotic and NATO framing.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Right and left sovereigntists differ on unions and bargaining, and the doctrine is about where authority sits.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The doctrine is silent on wage subsidies and its strands split on them.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Sovereigntists dislike externally imposed fiscal rules from the EU, but views on domestic rules vary by strand.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Trump's UN speech stresses reciprocal trade and national interest over global redistribution; inferred, as developing-country restructuring is not discussed.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Sovereigntists defend the national state and its institutions and wish to restore their authority, not destroy them.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The doctrine does not prescribe an economic system, though Thatcher's Bruges speech defends free enterprise.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The doctrine is silent on valuing nature, and strands differ.

sacred-nation.rationale: Thatcher's speech defends national identity and the nation as an enduring community, but sacredness is stronger than most sources state.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Mainstream right sovereigntists favour personal responsibility for loans, but the left strand differs; inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Sovereigntists treat the nation as a unit with a common interest; inferred, as the sources do not discuss internal colonialism.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Sovereigntists ground rights in national constitutions rather than universal bodies, but sources say little about human nature; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Strands split between defending national broadcasters and attacking state-funded media; sources are silent.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Sovereigntism is about where authority sits, and the sources say nothing on religious doctrine; adherents range from secular to devout.

farm-price-support.rationale: Right sovereigntists favour protectionism while Thatcherite ones favour free enterprise, so adherents split and the sources are silent on farm policy.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Sovereigntists stress national self-defence and the Bruges speech backs a strong national defence; keeping nuclear arms is inferred from that.

workers-own-party.rationale: The doctrine has no class programme; right sovereigntists oppose a labour party while left sovereigntists support one.

ban-fgm.rationale: Mainstream right-leaning sovereigntism stresses cultural continuity and law, so banning FGM is inferred, though the sources do not discuss it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Nothing in the doctrine opposes equal property rights for women, and the mainstream contemporary versions are liberal on this point; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The sources do not address how languages are named and it is not a sovereigntist question.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Sovereigntism has no environmental or tort-law position, and market-minded and state-minded adherents split.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: New sovereigntists ground authority in constitutional consent of the national people, which is inferred to leave no official role for hereditary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Trump's address rejects globalist environmental agreements in favour of national choice, so prioritising environment over liberty is inferred to be unwelcome.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Right-leaning sovereigntism emphasises law and order and national control of justice, so fixed sentences are inferred as favoured.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Sovereigntists stress border control and cultural continuity, and expect newcomers to integrate into the national culture and language.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Sovereigntism concerns the level of authority, not labour law; right variants favour right-to-work while left Eurosceptics defend union security.

voter-id.rationale: Border control and national citizenship as the basis of the political community are central to its best-known right-leaning versions, so proof of citizenship to vote is inferred as favoured, though the doctrine does not address it directly.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Sovereigntism takes no line on intra-religious precedence; it is about nation versus supranational bodies, and adherents differ across countries and faiths.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Sovereigntists hold that legitimacy rests on a national people's consent, which fits electoral democracy, but they stress that policy must remain nationally chosen; adherents are split on a purely procedural definition.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not a topic of the doctrine; sovereigntists range from social conservatives to secular nationalists, so no common position is inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The doctrine does not address internet shutdowns; a state-authority emphasis pulls one way and the democratic-accountability emphasis the other.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is outside the doctrine; the right-leaning strands distrust transfers while left strands defend the welfare state, so adherents split.

women-suffrage.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; equal political rights for women are accepted by mainstream sovereigntist parties and governments in Euro-Atlantic politics, inferred from that practice.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Mainstream sovereigntists in the Euro-Atlantic scope do not blame religion for women's oppression, and the right-leaning versions are often sympathetic to religious tradition; inferred, not stated in the sources.

race-social-construct.rationale: Race concepts are not addressed by the doctrine; the right-leaning strands include both civic nationalists who accept this and cultural-continuity voices who resist it.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Gender-equality institutions are not a sovereigntist concern; right strands tend to oppose new bureaucracy while some national governments run such agencies, so adherents split.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Sovereigntism is about where authority sits and takes no line on how property is first acquired.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Trump's UN speech rejected the ICC's claim of jurisdiction over Americans, and the CFR article gives the constitutionalist objection to such courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Sovereigntism has no doctrine on scripture; its strands range from religious to secular.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed; the strands differ on such guarantees.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from right-leaning strands' hostility to socialist planning, though the doctrine itself is only about authority.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national and popular sovereignty, which favours direct accountability to the people.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the defence of national identity and tradition, as in Thatcher's Bruges speech, which suits a national church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the demand for one supreme national authority, which weighs against ethnic territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the view that legitimacy rests on the consent of a people, which a local vote expresses.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from the defence of state borders and sovereignty against outside revision.

simple-living.rationale: The doctrine takes no line on lifestyle; strands differ.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: border control is central, but limits on settlement inside the country sit awkwardly with a unitary national state.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed; right and left strands differ.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Sovereigntists defend national identity and cultural continuity, but the sources do not frame it as a spiritual bond to ancestral land, so this is inferred.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The doctrine is about authority, not criminal justice; its constitutionalist wing stresses legal process, though some right-leaning adherents praised harsh drug wars, so this is a weak inference.

close-ties-china.rationale: Trump-era sovereigntism pursued reciprocal trade and distrust of rivals rather than closeness with China, an inference since the doctrine names no such alignment.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Nothing in the sources links sovereigntism to supporting kin abroad, and it stresses non-interference in other states as much as protecting nationals.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Sovereigntism assigns resources to the nation, not to all humanity equally, so a global common-ownership claim runs against it; inferred.

self-ownership.rationale: The best-known right-leaning strands lean individualist, but the doctrine does not address self-ownership, so this is inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Sovereigntism is about the level of authority, and adherents split on tax design.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Right and left sovereigntists differ on universal versus targeted welfare, and the doctrine itself takes no side.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Populist sovereigntists attack elites and parties, while Thatcherite and constitutionalist strands defend parliamentary institutions, so adherents are split.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The doctrine does not address business privileges; free-market and protectionist strands differ.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Sovereigntism does not address denominational politics, and strands range from secular French republicans to religious conservatives.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Contemporary sovereigntists defend cultural continuity while accepting modern economies, which is inferred from their national-identity stance.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Euro-Atlantic sovereigntist parties operate in states where this is already law and do not campaign against it; inferred.

national-resource-control.rationale: Keeping policy under national rather than supranational authority extends naturally to national control of resources, and Trump's UN speech links sovereignty to reciprocal, nation-first economic dealing.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Sovereigntism is about where authority sits; right and left strands differ on distribution, and the sources are silent.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Left-leaning sovereigntists support such taxes while right-leaning ones oppose them; the sources do not settle it.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The best-known versions are right-leaning and play down structural racism, but the sources do not discuss it; inferred.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The new sovereigntists stress consent and constitutional procedure as the source of legitimate law; inferred, not stated on unjust laws.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Sovereigntism has no position on automation; strands differ and the sources are silent.

multipolar-world.rationale: Trump's UN speech and the sovereigntist case favour independent nations over global governance, which fits several independent centres rather than one power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Thatcher's Bruges speech defends free enterprise and the best-known versions are right-leaning; inferred, with left strands dissenting.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Trump's UN speech presents patriotism as serving citizens, and the RN pairs national and popular sovereignty (s5); strands differ on the economics.

material-over-identity.rationale: Sovereigntism is a stance on authority; adherents split on whether economics or culture should come first.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Sovereigntism is not communist and its best-known strands are market-friendly; inferred, not discussed.

missingStatements.text: A country's constitution and laws should take precedence over international law and treaty obligations.
missingStatements.rationale: The new sovereigntists hold that the Constitution recognises no superior legal authority, and US ratification attaches reservations to preserve its supremacy.

missingStatements.text: International courts and treaty-monitoring bodies should have no authority over a country's own citizens or officials.
missingStatements.rationale: Trump's UN speech says the ICC has no jurisdiction, legitimacy or authority, and sovereigntists object to UN rapporteurs and judicial networks.

notes: Strand differences: left sovereigntists (some Eurosceptic left and Quebec) differ on economics and immigration; Russian and archeo-sovereigntist variants reject the Western order more radically. Wikipedia's article is thinly sourced in places, so the profile leans on the CFR account and primary speeches.
